We are seeking a passionate, energetic, and dedicated Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) to join our team in the Key Biscayne area.

We are looking for someone with flexible availability on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, with the ability to accommodate both morning and afternoon sessions. This particular opportunity will initially involve a combination of morning and afternoon home-based sessions, with an anticipated transition to the school setting beginning in the new year. As an RBT, you will work closely with an individual with autism and/or other developmental needs, implementing evidence-based behavioral interventions under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). Your role is vital in helping clients develop meaningful skills, increase independence, and enhance their overall quality of life.

This paid position offers an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference while gaining valuable experience in applied behavior analysis and special education.

Responsibilities

• Implement individualized behavior intervention plans based on ABA (Applied Behavior Analysis) principles to support clients’ developmental goals.

• Collect and record data on client progress, behavior patterns, and skill acquisition to inform ongoing treatment strategies.

• Assist clients with activities of daily living (ADLs), such as grooming, dressing, eating, and communication skills, promoting independence.

• Support clients during therapy sessions by teaching new skills and managing challenging behaviors through positive reinforcement techniques.

• Maintain accurate and confidential clinical documentation, including progress notes and treatment records, in compliance with HIPAA regulations.

• Collaborate with BCBA supervisors and team members to implement and adapt interventions as needed for optimal client outcomes.

• Foster a safe, supportive environment that encourages growth, patience, and respect for each individual's unique needs.

Experience & Qualifications

• Prior experience working with children or individuals with developmental disabilities is preferred.

• Knowledge of behavioral therapy techniques, particularly Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), is desirable.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to teach effectively in a one-on-one setting are essential.

• A compassionate attitude, patience, flexibility, and resilience when supporting clients through behavioral challenges.

• Ability to work independently while maintaining consistent communication and collaboration with the supervising BCBA.

Position Details

• Location: Key Biscayne, FL

• Days: Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays

• Availability: Flexible availability across morning and afternoon hours is required.

Job Description

Job Description Position Overview A Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) is responsible for providing one-on-one behavioral interventions to individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other developmental disabilities. Under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), the RBT implements treatment plans using Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) techniques to promote skill development and reduce challenging behaviors.

Responsibilities
• Implement Behavior Plans: Follow treatment plans designed by the BCBA to help clients develop skills and manage behaviors.
• Direct Client Interaction: Work one-on-one with clients in home, school, clinic, or community settings.
• Data Collection: Timely and accurately record and track progress based on behavioral data.
• Skill Development: Help clients improve in areas such as communication, social skills, daily living skills, and academics.
• Crisis Management: Use de-escalation techniques to handle challenging behaviors safely.
• Parent & Caregiver Training: Assist families by providing strategies to reinforce skills outside of sessions.
• Collaboration: Communicate with BCBAs, teachers, therapists, and families to ensure consistent implementation of interventions.
• Ethical Compliance: Follow all Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB) guidelines, HIPAA regulations, and company policies on ethical compliance.

Requirements, Qualifications & Skills
• Active RBT certification from the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).
• High school diploma or equivalent
• Experience working with children, individuals with ASD or developmental disabilities is preferred.
• Ability to pass a background check and obtain CPR certification.
• Strong communication and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Work Environment/Physical Demands
• This is a field-based role that requires travel to various client locations, including homes, schools, and clinics.
• Regularly involves standing, walking, bending, and engaging with clients in active environments.
• This job requires reliable transportation for travel up to 18 miles from employee’s home to field location.
• May involve working afternoons, evenings, or weekends based on client needs.

Our Benefits:
At The Behaviorists, we value our team members and their well-being. Our benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, paid holidays, and access to voluntary benefits such as disability coverage. We also offer a 401(k) Retirement benefit with company match.

• Skill Development: Help clients improve in areas such as communication, social skills, daily living skills, and academics.
• Crisis Management: Use de-escalation techniques to handle challenging behaviors safely.
• Parent & Caregiver Training: Assist families by providing strategies to reinforce skills outside of sessions.
• Collaboration: Communicate with BCBAs, teachers, therapists, and families to ensure consistent implementation of interventions.
• Ethical Compliance: Follow all Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB) guidelines, HIPAA regulations, and company policies on ethical compliance.

Requirements, Qualifications & Skills

• High school diploma or equivalent
• Experience working with children, individuals with ASD or developmental disabilities is preferred.
• Ability to pass a background check and obtain CPR certification.
• Strong communication and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

• This is a field-based role that requires travel to various client locations, including homes, schools, and clinics.

Position Overview

A Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) is responsible for providing one-on-one behavioral interventions to individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other developmental disabilities. Under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), the RBT implements treatment plans using Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) techniques to promote skill development and reduce challenging behaviors.

Responsibilities

• Implement Behavior Plans: Follow treatment plans designed by the BCBA to help clients develop skills and manage behaviors.

• Direct Client Interaction: Work one-on-one with clients in home, school, clinic, or community settings.

• Data Collection: Timely and accurately record and track progress based on behavioral data.

• Skill Development: Help clients improve in areas such as communication, social skills, daily living skills, and academics.

• Crisis Management: Use de-escalation techniques to handle challenging behaviors safely.

• Parent & Caregiver Training: Assist families by providing strategies to reinforce skills outside of sessions.

• Collaboration: Communicate with BCBAs, teachers, therapists, and families to ensure consistent implementation of interventions.

• Ethical Compliance: Follow all Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB) guidelines, HIPAA regulations, and company policies on ethical compliance.

Requirements, Qualifications & Skills

• Active RBT certification from the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).

• High school diploma or equivalent

• Ability to pass a background check and obtain CPR certification.

• Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Work Environment/Physical Demands

• This is a field-based role that requires travel to various client locations, including homes, schools, and clinics.

• Regularly involves standing, walking, bending, and engaging with clients in active environments.

• This job requires reliable transportation for travel up to 18 miles from employee’s home to field location.

• May involve working afternoons, evenings, or weekends based on client needs.

At The Behaviorists, we value our team members and their well-being. Our benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, paid holidays, and access to voluntary benefits such as disability coverage. We also offer a 401(k) Retirement benefit with company match.

Under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), the RBT implements treatment plans using Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) techniques to promote skill development and reduce challenging behaviors.

Responsibilities

• Implement Behavior Plans: Follow treatment plans designed by the BCBA to help clients develop skills and manage behaviors.

• Direct Client Interaction: Work one-on-one with clients in home, school, clinic, or community settings.

• Data Collection: Timely and accurately record and track progress based on behavioral data.

• Skill Development: Help clients improve in areas such as communication, social skills, daily living skills, and academics.

• Crisis Management: Use de-escalation techniques to handle challenging behaviors safely.

• Parent & Caregiver Training: Assist families by providing strategies to reinforce skills outside of sessions.

• Collaboration: Communicate with BCBAs, teachers, therapists, and families to ensure consistent implementation of interventions.

• Ethical Compliance: Follow all Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB) guidelines, HIPAA regulations, and company policies on ethical compliance.

Requirements, Qualifications & Skills

• Active RBT certification from the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).

• High school diploma or equivalent

• Experience working with children, individuals with ASD or developmental disabilities is preferred.

• Ability to pass a background check and obtain CPR certification.

• Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Work Environment/Physical Demands

• This is a field-based role that requires travel to various client locations, including homes, schools, and clinics.

• Regularly involves standing, walking, bending, and engaging with clients in active environments.

• This job requires reliable transportation for travel up to 18 miles from employee’s home to field location.

• May involve working afternoons, evenings, or weekends based on client needs.

Our Benefits:

At The Behaviorists, we value our team members and their well-being. Our benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, paid holidays, and access to voluntary benefits such as disability coverage. We also offer a 401(k) Retirement benefit with company match.

Position Overview

A Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) is responsible for providing one-on-one behavioral interventions to individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other developmental disabilities. Under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), the RBT implements treatment plans using Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) techniques to promote skill development and reduce challenging behaviors.

Responsibilities

• Implement Behavior Plans: Follow treatment plans designed by the BCBA to help clients develop skills and manage behaviors.

• Direct Client Interaction: Work one-on-one with clients in home, school, clinic, or community settings.

• Data Collection: Timely and accurately record and track progress based on behavioral data.

• Skill Development: Help clients improve in areas such as communication, social skills, daily living skills, and academics.

• Crisis Management: Use de-escalation techniques to handle challenging behaviors safely.

• Parent & Caregiver Training: Assist families by providing strategies to reinforce skills outside of sessions.

• Collaboration: Communicate with BCBAs, teachers, therapists, and families to ensure consistent implementation of interventions.

• Ethical Compliance: Follow all Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB) guidelines, HIPAA regulations, and company policies on ethical compliance.

Requirements, Qualifications & Skills

• Active RBT certification from the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).

• High school diploma or equivalent

• Experience working with children, individuals with ASD or developmental disabilities is preferred.

• Ability to pass a background check and obtain CPR certification.

• Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Work Environment/Physical Demands

• This is a field-based role that requires travel to various client locations, including homes, schools, and clinics.

• Regularly involves standing, walking, bending, and engaging with clients in active environments.

• This job requires reliable transportation for travel up to 18 miles from employee’s home to field location.

• May involve working afternoons, evenings, or weekends based on client needs.

Our Benefits:

At The Behaviorists, we value our team members and their well-being. Our benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, paid holidays, and access to voluntary benefits such as disability coverage. We also offer a 401(k) Retirement benefit with company match.

Position Overview

A Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) is responsible for providing one-on-one behavioral interventions to individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other developmental disabilities. Under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), the RBT implements treatment plans using Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) techniques to promote skill development and reduce challenging behaviors.

Responsibilities

• Implement Behavior Plans: Follow treatment plans designed by the BCBA to help clients develop skills and manage behaviors.

• Direct Client Interaction: Work one-on-one with clients in home, school, clinic, or community settings.

• Data Collection: Timely and accurately record and track progress based on behavioral data.

• Skill Development: Help clients improve in areas such as communication, social skills, daily living skills, and academics.

• Crisis Management: Use de-escalation techniques to handle challenging behaviors safely.

• Parent & Caregiver Training: Assist families by providing strategies to reinforce skills outside of sessions.

• Collaboration: Communicate with BCBAs, teachers, therapists, and families to ensure consistent implementation of interventions.

• Ethical Compliance: Follow all Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB) guidelines, HIPAA regulations, and company policies on ethical compliance.

Requirements, Qualifications & Skills

• Active RBT certification from the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).

• High school diploma or equivalent

• Experience working with children, individuals with ASD or developmental disabilities is preferred.

• Ability to pass a background check and obtain CPR certification.

• Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Work Environment/Physical Demands

• This is a field-based role that requires travel to various client locations, including homes, schools, and clinics.

• Regularly involves standing, walking, bending, and engaging with clients in active environments.

• This job requires reliable transportation for travel up to 18 miles from employee’s home to field location.

• May involve working afternoons, evenings, or weekends based on client needs.

Our Benefits:

At The Behaviorists, we value our team members and their well-being. Our benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, paid holidays, and access to voluntary benefits such as disability coverage. We also offer a 401(k) Retirement benefit with company match.

Position Overview: Behaviorial Technician will provide direct care to individuals, primarily focusing on supporting youth in achieving their therapeutic and developmental goals. This role involves maintaining a therapeutic environment through trauma-informed care, crisis management, and behavioral interventions. The position requires compassion, creativity, and a commitment to ensuring the safety and well-being of each child.

Key Responsibilities:

• Therapeutic Interactions:

• Foster positive, therapeutic relationships with youth, ensuring safety and stability. Apply trauma-informed care and use strength-based approaches in all interactions. Assist children with daily routines, including meals, school, social activities, and personal hygiene as part of their treatment plans.

• Behavior Management:

Implement behavior management strategies and protocols, including individualized crisis intervention plans, to facilitate positive behavioral outcomes. Provide direct supervision during high-risk activities or when 1:1 supervision is required.

• Youth Development & Support:

Assist children with academic support, including homework, social skills development, emotional regulation, and life skills training. Model appropriate behaviors and help guide children in recreational activities and group instruction as outlined in their Individual Treatment Plans (ITP).Ensure the facility is secure and well-maintained. Attend regular staff meetings, clinical meetings, and family support sessions to contribute to comprehensive care planning. Complete all mandatory training, including crisis intervention, abuse reporting, child care activities, and any other relevant professional development programs. Remain current with required certifications such as CPR, de-escalation, and restraint training. Demonstrate understanding and respect for the cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds of the youth and families served. Provide care in a culturally competent manner, ensuring all children’s needs are addressed. Accurately document client progress, behavioral incidents, and other required reports. Ensure all documentation is up-to-date, compliant with regulations, and submitted in a timely manner. Assist with transporting children to and from activities, as needed. Maintain confidentiality, boundaries and respect client privacy at all times. Perform other duties as assigned by management.

Registered Behavior Technician (RBT)

Butterfly Effects' Mission is to make a socially significant change in the lives of children and families by hiring passionate, caring people to serve children and families affected by autism.

We are seeking dedicated Registered Behavior Technicians, entry-level and experienced, to directly assist children with autism in honing vital skills like communication, social interaction, and self-care. Join us in collaborating with families to execute ABA based behavior intervention plans.

Are you passionate about positively impacting the lives of children and families? Explore our fulfilling part-time role at Butterfly Effects!

Why Work at Butterfly Effects?

• Competitive Compensation: Hourly, based on your experience, education, and certifications.

• Part-Time Flexibility: 9-20 hours per week, providing the ideal work-life balance.

• Impactful Work: Contribute to lifelong changes in a child's life.

• Career Growth: Available for educational and training support, with opportunities to become an Registered Behavior Technician or to grow towards gaining a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), aided by our guidance and financial assistance.

• Supportive Environment: Join a team focused on bringing calm, protection, and joy to families affected by autism.

What Would You Be Doing?

• Implements individualized treatment plans under the direction of a Board-Certified Behavioral Analyst (BCBA).

• Observes, records, and reports on client's progress, as well as the condition and behavior of the client daily.

• Manages challenging behaviors.

• Applies behavioral principles consistently in all interactions with clients.

• Assists clients, as needed, to acquire academic and/or appropriate life skills.

• Communicates in a professional and respectful manner with parents, behavior analysts/consultants, trainers, and clients.

• Functions as an active member of the treatment team.

• Completes daily paperwork and data collection notes in a detailed, accurate, consistent and timely manner through our on-line database.

• Actively participates in continuous training programs designed to increase overall skills.

• Maintains confidentiality of client information.

• Follows BE policies and procedures.

What Do You Bring to the Role?

• Education: High school diploma or equivalent.

• Certification: Active RBT Certification with Medicaid Credentials.

• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with children.

• Positive Attitude: Strong interpersonal skills for working with children and families.

• Experience: Prior experience with children is advantageous.

• Continuous Learning: Interest in ongoing development.

• Transportation: Must have reliable transportation.

• Background: Must be able to satisfactorily pass a company background check.

Follow this link to get a better understanding of your role:

Physical Requirements:

This role involves working in natural environments, occasionally requiring lifting or moving up to 50 lbs. and maintaining various postures for extended periods.

Who Are We?

Butterfly Effects has served more than 15,000 families since our inception in 2005. We have a long history of improving the lives of children and families affected by autism spectrum disorder through our family-centric applied behavior analysis (ABA) approach. Our mission is to deliver ABA treatment in partnership with families affected by autism to foster a more joyous life.

Our butterfly logo was chosen as a symbol of love, rebirth, and metamorphosis. Together, the name and logo represent our common purpose and deep commitment to helping families create lasting change through individualized ABA therapy.
